posts.title: Back squats beat hip thrusts for basketball jumps
posts.excerpt: A Frontiers in Physiology study published November 4 found that four sets of three back squats at 80% of one-rep max, followed by eight minutes of rest, lifted countermovement and approach jumps in…
posts.body: A [Frontiers in Physiology study published November 4](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/physiology/articles/10.3389/fphys.2026.1950623/full) found that four sets of three back squats at 80% of one-rep max, followed by eight minutes of rest, lifted countermovement and approach jumps in 20 male collegiate basketball players. Hip thrusts at the same load showed no significant edge over a basketball-specific warm-up.

posts.excerpt: A Frontiers in Public Health study published November 5 found that, among 74 competitive middle- and long-distance runners, more rest days in the preceding week were linked to lower odds of an injury…
posts.body: A [Frontiers in Public Health study published November 5](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/public-health/articles/10.3389/fpubh.2026.1990002/full) found that, among 74 competitive middle- and long-distance runners, more rest days in the preceding week were linked to lower odds of an injury label.
